ShortDescription.Value: Every terrain-tool stroke costs money, priced by the real volume of earth you move - with a live cost tooltip while you drag.

Publish.LongDescription:
**Terraform Costs**
Ever felt like Cities: Skylines II's terrain tools are basically free money-printing machines for flattening an entire mountain range before you've even placed your first road? This brings back the classic Cities: Skylines (1) "Terraform Tool" experience: every raise, lower, level, soften and slope stroke costs money, priced by how much earth you're actually moving. Run out of money and the brush just stops - no debt, no drama.
- Price is based on the *real, measured* volume of terrain moved for all 4 terrain tools (Raise/Lower, Level, Soften, Slope) - not just brush size and a timer. - A live tooltip while you drag shows the moved volume (m³) and the running cost (₡) for the current stroke, plus the price per 100 m³. - Every cubic metre costs the same no matter which tool moved it (adjustable Level/Soften/Slope price factor). - Optional refund for the part of a stroke that lowers terrain (0% by default). - Free in the map editor, as it should be. Unlimited-money games are unaffected. - Fully adjustable in Options: enable/disable, 0-10x price multiplier, Level/Soften/Slope price factor, lowering refund %. - English and German localisation.
**Compatibility:** Hard Mode Continued also charges for terraforming - if you run both, you'll be charged by both, so pick one if you don't want double charges. TerraformCost detects it and shows a warning in Options.
Building/road/water-tool terrain smoothing is never charged - only deliberate use of the Landscaping terrain tool itself.
